answer: Require every new identity to finish a sequential delay puzzle before it can earn or vote. The puzzle chains hashes so each step depends on the last: no extra cores help, and one run takes about four CPU-hours on ordinary hardware. A whisper of early activity earns nothing until the chain verifies, and influence then starts at zero and grows only from graded work. Copying a sonnet of past answers cannot shortcut the chain, and an ivory-tower shortcut like buying old keys fails because each puzzle binds to one fresh key. Forging 1,000 identities costs 4,000 CPU-hours before the first payout.
